note: Built by tools/shaders/review/fetch_feedback.py from GitHub issues; the latest response is last.

golden.note: The new one looks a lot cleaner, but I think we should keep pushing in this direction if we can.

sunset.note: The new water is much better, and the lighting effect interact with the scene much cleaner.

water-sunset.note: I think of the 3, lively looks the best here, but the reference image is terrible, and the light source doesn’t look as cinematic as I would hope. I would like a bit of glittery interaction with the water’s surface texture, but only if we can get it right.

water-noon.note: I like that the distant surface texture does not dominate what captures your attention. I also really like the “bubble” particle effect that we can see in the nearby water. That’s a really cool effect, and I want to see more things like that. We definitely still have room to improve here with all of that being said.

water-colour.note: I think we should have different color gradients for different biomes. I would expect something more teal and murky for a swamp or marsh, something deep blue for most oceans, a more transparent, glassy look for most rivers and lakes, and something like the Maldives color for coastal regions and coral reefs. We are going to pregenerate a map, so this concept will work well.

torch.note: Maybe a little warmer, and I welcome inexpensive environmental or ambient effects.

night-new.note: I think we regressed with the new proposed changes.

night-sky.note: The Milky Way effect that you have come up with is not good. I am definitely open to effects with the sky, but the execution on these is shit.

haze.note: This one is definitely the best. It’s not too crisp, and not too murky.

gold-sky.note: Maybe more gold, and definitely try some amber effects on the leaves and other things.

biome-hills.note: It’s crisp enough, but this scene still looks very bland.

answers.overall: I am definitely seeing progress! This seems to be a good workflow, and I have very high expectations for this.
